comparison.method: Git blob SHA comparison by relative path against the exact recorded upstream template commit

interpretation.byteIdenticalFiles: These seven files have identical Git blob content at the compared relative paths.
interpretation.modifiedFiles: Different content at the same path; this comparison does not distinguish permitted configuration/customization from upstream source modification.
interpretation.localOnlyFiles: Not present at the compared upstream paths; these may be LuckRead-owned code, separately reused upstream material, assets, or generated files. Each copied/adapted source still requires its own provenance and license record.
interpretation.upstreamOnlyFiles: Files present in the upstream template but absent at the same W01 relative path; omission alone is not evidence of a violation.
interpretation.limitation: This is a path-and-blob comparison against one historical template snapshot, not a complete semantic source audit or proof that all local-only code is original.

requiredFollowUp: Classify the 24 same-path modifications as configuration, supported extension, generated output, or source-level modification.
Establish source and license records for copied/adapted local-only code, including the separately documented ccrsxx/twitter-clone MIT adaptations.
Reconcile the historical D1 template baseline with the current Neon target without copying upstream D1 runtime code back into the application.

classification.assessment: Focused review of key files indicates application/template customization through Payload configuration, Collections, hooks, plugins and generated artifacts; no modified Payload Core implementation or private Payload fork was found in the reviewed files. This is not a complete line-by-line semantic audit of every W01-only file.

openFinding.assessment: Current payload.config.ts uses the LuckRead-owned Neon adapter, but package placement retains a D1 adapter runtime dependency and places the Postgres adapter in devDependencies. Do not change without W01 runtime/build validation.

thirdPartyAttribution.assessment: Notices preserve MIT attribution and identify reused frontend patterns; full file-by-file copied-source mapping and exact upstream license revision verification remain open.
